A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same auxiliary-variable MCMC framework and algorithms. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v3 Section 5 and Appendix F report original Gaussian and regression simulations and MNIST classification experiments, including MSE, ESS/s and test accuracy.

after.justification: v4 Section 5 and Appendix G retain original empirical results and add distributional correctness checks, a larger regression experiment and minibatch sensitivity results.

M1.justification: v3 Algorithms 4–6 correspond to v4 Algorithms 1–3, retaining the same auxiliary-variable transition, locally balanced PoissonMH proposals and Tuna–SGLD correction. Mathematical repairs and revised implementation disclosures do not establish a change to these proposed procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate heterogeneous truncated Gaussian sampling, robust linear regression in 10 and 50 dimensions, and MNIST classification of 3s/5s and 7s/9s. The added sample-size configuration, correctness checks and minibatch sweeps retain these data families and tasks.

E2.justification: SGLD is newly evaluated in the Gaussian and 10-dimensional regression MSE plots and the new KS comparison. Corresponding ESS tables retain their comparator sets. PoissonMH-Barker/MALA and Poisson–Barker/MALA denote the same methods across versions.

E3.justification: v4 adds rejection-sampling references, matched computation budgets, 20% burn-in and dimensionwise two-sample KS statistics in Section 5.4. Additional configurations include 200,000 regression samples and gradient minibatches of 20, 64 and 128. The added regression experiment inconsistently labels HMC as five steps in Table 6 and ten in Figure 6, leaving that setting unresolved.

E4.justification: Section 5.4/Table 3 adds reference-sample KS checks that extend v3's moment-based validation. Appendix G.4/Figure 12 adds joint gradient-minibatch-size and step-size sensitivity experiments for Tuna–SGLD. These materially expand validation; the HMC-leapfrog, higher-dimensional and earlier step-size analyses were already present in v3.

E5.justification: Reported averaging for the main Gaussian and 10-dimensional regression results changes from 10 to 100 runs. Retained 50-dimensional and HMC-leapfrog comparisons still report 10 runs. No seed information, confidence intervals or significance reporting is added; table minima and maxima remain summaries across dimensions.

E6.justification: Main synthetic MSE curves and ESS/s values are revised. For example, best median Poisson–MALA ESS/s in regression changes from 591.6 to 491.8 in Table 2, alongside changed run averaging. New KS, larger-sample and minibatch-sensitivity results are reported. The retained 50-dimensional table also corrects MH's Best entry from (0.00, 0.10, 0.12) to (0.08, 0.10, 0.13).

T1.justification: v4 weakens one branch of the PoissonMH spectral-gap guarantee and replaces its flawed product-TV derivation (v3 Proposition 5/Appendix A.9; v4 Proposition 4/Appendix B.9). It also adds the missing uniform supremum in Theorem 2, corrects KL exponent signs, restores the regression tempering factor and replaces the invalid logistic-bound argument with a mean-value argument. These revise mathematical claims and reasoning.

C1.justification: The main claims of unification, exact gradient-informed minibatch sampling and improved computational efficiency remain. v4 drops v3's introductory assertion that its framework is more comprehensive than existing approaches and explicitly identifies its construction as an instance of involutive MCMC, narrowing the novelty positioning.

C2.justification: v4 adds explicit limitations concerning unavailable or loose bounds and hyperparameter dependence, interprets SGLD's plateau as consistent with fixed-step bias, and explains the preference for small gradient minibatches. Conversely, v3 Section 4.5's discussion of uninformative spectral-gap comparisons and weaker comparison theories is removed.

D1.justification: v4 changes the code-repository pointer, documents SGLD's batch size of 512 and adds Tuna–SGLD tuning guidance. It omits v3's Julia implementation statement and gradient-norm clipping threshold of 2. These omissions establish reduced disclosure, not that the implementation language or clipping procedure actually changed.

R1.justification: The broad literature review is substantially reduced, removing discussion and citations concerning exchange extensions, several subsampling approaches and weak-Poincaré comparisons. v4 instead develops explicit distinctions from pseudo-marginal and PDMP samplers and adds Neklyudov et al. (2020), with a formal connection to involutive MCMC.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work are extensively condensed and rewritten. Baseline pseudocode, worked examples and spectral-gap development move to appendices; standalone notation, organization and theory-outlook sections disappear. The correctness-check section and acknowledgment/impact material are added, and author order changes.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a two-column main text and replaces full main-text ESS tables with compact Best summaries, relocating detailed tables and the Gaussian plot to the appendix. It removes the workflow and MNIST-example illustrations, redraws synthetic plots with SGLD, and adds correctness, larger-sample and tuning displays. Existing MNIST and most other appendix plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 improves credibility through specific mathematical repairs, reference-sample correctness checks, tuning analyses and 100-run averages for the main synthetic experiments. These provide a supported net gain. The gain is limited by removal of the theoretical-limitations discussion and implementation disclosures, together with inconsistent HMC settings in the new 200,000-sample experiment.
